Post Apocalyptic type environment where either civilization exists above the buried ruins of an older civilization or in the catacombs beneath them. More or less a modified version of the Fallout idea, that and playing too much Civilization (raiding ruins).

Above The tribes subsist in the blasted lands among the hills and overgrown forests of the wildlands. Mountains of crumbling stone and twisted rock so hard it cannot break dot the landscape. In these tombs of days long past exist the only scraps of the old world. The technologies and materials so commonplace back then have been lost for centuries, the oils and gasses once rent from the earth were depleted long before the collapse.

The tribes survive on the outskirts of the these monuments to man's hubris but dare not venture inside too often nor stray too far from their protective shadow. When tools, weapons, or essential goods are broken or used beyond repair salvagers must venture into the cities to collect what is needed. Beyond the perimeter of the cities there is a plentiful harvest of game, and predators. Without vehicles, horses, or most domesticated animals the people of the tribes have been reduced to primitive hunter gatherer society. Their expeditions into the rock jungles often meet fierce resistance from the shadow men of the underground.

Below The people live their lives in the burrows beneath the collapse. Above lie the remnants of days long since past. The Buried avoid the surface as it is never safe. Sadly, they cannot grow enough food in the dark caverns beneath the old cities. A hobbled together patchwork of grow lights, water storage batteries, and solar cells allow the Buried to eek out an existence. Though the terrors of the open sky, huge predatory beasts and roaming packs of feral beasts, stay away from the catacombs and sewer complexes there is the ever present threat of the half-mad cannibal tribesmen. While the Buried have the means to educate and train they cannot support the numbers the tribal hordes throw in their slaving parties.

Combination I am thinking this would be an interesting scenario to run with multiple DMs. One of the groups DMs would run the surface campaign and focus on the more primitive and beastial aspects. The other DM would focus on the base building and technical/cyber punk aspects of the Buried.

Some "global" events could occur in both games, i.e. the rupture of a chemical storage plant near a major source of water or a new apex predator is introduced to the ecology. Adding some elements of genetically altered super predators or toxic hazards would greatly increase the tense factor. In addition neither party should have sufficient food or water to really thrive.

The tribal party would have more pressing worries about rival tribes, beasts, and perhaps even roving robotic crazies. The Buried would have issues with structural integrity/collapse, fires, etc.
Pillaging the ruins of an ancient civilization.

If the two parties occur in the same city at the same time you might get some unpleasant cross party killing, probably best to have the two games run in separate cities or offset by a few years. No sense in ruining a good group with PKs.
